value: Acid is a general term for a sour-tasting ingredient that adds tartness and helps control pH in food. The specific type is usually named elsewhere on the label.
Acidity regulator is a class of additives that adjusts how acidic or alkaline a food is, helping to control tartness, stability and pH.
Agave syrup is a liquid sweetener made by processing sap from the agave plant, and it is used to add sweetness to beverages, sauces and baked goods.
Ethyl alcohol produced by fermenting sugars from grains or fruit, used in the product as a solvent and to carry flavors.
The dried, ground berry of a tropical evergreen tree, with a flavor that resembles a blend of cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg, used as a spice.
The edible seed of the almond tree, sold whole, sliced or ground. It is used for crunch, flavor and texture in foods.
Small, salt-cured fish from the herring family, usually packed in oil or brine, that adds a deep, savory umami flavor to sauces, dressings and pastes.
A mixture of substances added in small amounts to powdered foods to keep particles from clumping together and help them pour freely.
Antioxidant is a class of additive that slows the reaction of fats and oils with oxygen, helping to preserve the food's flavor and color over time.
Apples are the fruit of the apple tree, and in food they add natural sweetness, tartness, and moisture in both whole and processed forms.
The liquid pressed or extracted from apples, usually clarified and sometimes concentrated. It is used as a natural sweetener and flavoring in beverages, baked goods, and other foods.
Apple juice that has been concentrated by removing water and then reconstituted, used as a sweetener and flavoring.
Apple puree is apples cooked and blended into a smooth, thick pulp. It adds fruit flavor, sweetness and moisture to foods.
The small orange fruit of a tree related to the peach, used fresh, dried or as puree or juice to add sweet-tart fruit flavor to foods.
Artificial flavor is a manufactured substance, made by chemical synthesis rather than from a natural source, that is added to give a food a specific taste or aroma.
A hard Italian cow's milk cheese with a nutty, slightly sharp flavor, used as a seasoning or eaten on its own.
Autolyzed yeast extract is a flavor ingredient made by breaking down yeast cells with their own enzymes and then concentrating the liquid. It is used to add savory, brothy flavor to foods.
The fleshy green fruit of an avocado tree, used in the product for its creamy texture and mild flavor.
An oil pressed from the flesh of avocado fruit, used for cooking and in dressings because it is stable at high heat and has a mild flavor.
Bacon is pork belly that has been cured, typically with salt and other ingredients, and often smoked, and it is used to add a salty, smoky, savory flavor.
A dry leavening agent made of an alkaline ingredient, an acid, and a starch filler. When moistened and heated, it releases carbon dioxide gas that makes batters and doughs rise.
Balsamic vinegar is a vinegar made from fermented grape must that is aged, used to add a sweet, tangy and tart flavor to dressings and sauces.
Banana is the fruit of the banana plant, and in foods it is used in pieces, puree or flavor to add sweetness, moisture and its characteristic taste.
Barley is a cereal grain from the grass family, used whole, hulled, or processed into flakes and flour. In food it adds bulk, chewy texture, and a mild, toasty flavor.
Barley malt extract is a syrupy liquid made by soaking and sprouting barley grain and then concentrating the resulting sugars, used as a sweetener and flavoring in foods.
Flour made from barley that has been allowed to sprout and then dried, which adds malty flavor and color to baked goods.
Basil is an aromatic green herb from the mint family whose leaves are dried or chopped and added to food to give a sweet, peppery flavor.
Bay leaf is the dried leaf of the bay laurel tree, used as a herb to add a mild, aromatic flavor to savory dishes.
Beans are the edible seeds of legume plants, eaten whole, mashed or ground into flour. They add protein, fiber and substance to many foods.
The flesh of cattle, used as a meat ingredient in prepared foods for its flavor and protein.
A savory liquid made by simmering beef and bones with vegetables and seasonings, used as a base for soups, sauces and gravies.
Beet is the root of a plant in the goosefoot family, cooked or used as a vegetable. In food it adds earthy flavor and a deep red color.
Bell peppers are the fruit of the Capsicum annuum plant, typically sweet and mild with no capsaicin heat. They are used as a vegetable ingredient, dried, powdered, or as a flavoring and coloring.
A group of bacteria, related to Bifidobacterium, that is added to fermented dairy products as a culture that helps produce acidity and flavor.
A B-vitamin, also called vitamin B7 or vitamin H, that is added to foods as a nutrient and helps the body process fats, carbohydrates, and proteins.
The small, dark seeds of the black bean plant, sold dried or canned. In food they add bulk, color and a mild, earthy flavor.
The dried, ground fruit of the pepper vine, used as a spice to add a sharp, pungent flavor to savory foods.
Leaves of the tea plant that have been fermented and dried, used to brew a dark, astringent beverage and to flavor foods.
Blackberries are the dark, juicy fruit of bramble plants, used fresh, frozen or as puree to add tart-sweet fruit flavor and color.
Blue cheese is a cheese made from cow, sheep or goat milk and cultured with Penicillium mold, which gives it a sharp, tangy flavor and blue veining.
The small round blue or purple berry of a shrub in the Vaccinium genus. It is eaten fresh or used frozen, dried, or as a purée to flavor foods such as baked goods, cereals, and beverages.
The edible seeds of a large tropical tree native to South America, with a rich, buttery flavor and a high natural oil content, used whole, chopped or as nut butter.
Dried, ground bread pieces used as a coating for frying and baking or as a filler. They add crunch and help bind other ingredients together.
Green flowering vegetable from the cabbage family, with tight clusters of buds on thick stems, eaten cooked or raw.
Broth is a flavorful liquid made by simmering meat, bones, poultry or vegetables in water, used as a base for soups, sauces and cooking.
Brown rice is whole-grain rice that has had only its tough outer hull removed, leaving the bran layer intact. It is cooked and eaten as a grain or ground into flour.

Brown rice flour is a fine powder made by milling whole brown rice grains, bran and germ included. It is used as a gluten-free flour that adds body and a mild, nutty flavor to baked and processed foods.
Brown rice syrup is a sweetener made by breaking down the starches in brown rice with enzymes, producing a thick liquid that adds sweetness and moisture.
Sugar crystals that retain some molasses, giving them a moist texture and a caramel-like flavor. It is used to sweeten and color foods.
Butter is a solid dairy fat made by churning cream, used for flavor, richness and texture in cooking and baking.
Natural butter flavor is a flavoring derived from natural sources such as dairy ingredients, produced through processes like fermentation or heating. It adds a buttery taste to foods.
Butter oil is the fat portion of butter, separated from the milk solids and water, and it is used to add rich dairy flavor and fat to foods.
The liquid left after butter is churned from cream, or a cultured dairy product made with lactic acid bacteria, used for tanginess and tenderness in baking.
The dried solids left after the liquid is removed from cultured or fermented milk, used to add tangy dairy flavor and creamy texture to baked goods and mixes.
Cabbage is a leafy vegetable from the brassica family, with tightly packed layers that are used fresh, cooked, or fermented in foods.
Caffeine is a bitter, naturally occurring stimulant compound found in coffee, tea and cacao, added to some foods and drinks for its flavor and effect.
Calcium is a mineral element used in food as an additive, often in the form of calcium salts. It can serve as a firming agent, a leavening agent or a nutrient fortifier.
Milk protein, casein, combined with calcium, used as an emulsifier, binder and source of protein in food.
A salt of pantothenic acid, one of the B vitamins, produced for use as a vitamin additive. It is added to foods to supply this nutrient.
Sucrose extracted from sugarcane and refined into white or brown crystals that sweetens foods and helps with texture and browning.
A sweet liquid made by dissolving sugar extracted from sugarcane in water, often with some of the cane's natural flavor retained. It is used as a sweetener in foods and drinks.
Canola is a plant grown from rapeseed bred for low erucic acid, and its seed is pressed to make a mild-tasting cooking oil.
An edible oil pressed from seeds of the canola plant, a variety of rapeseed, that is used for cooking, frying and in processed foods.
Carbonated water is plain water infused with carbon dioxide gas under pressure, which creates bubbles. It is used to give drinks their fizz.
The dried seed pods of a plant in the ginger family, whose aromatic seeds are ground or used whole to add a warm, sweet, citrusy spice flavor.
A root vegetable that is sweet and crunchy, used fresh, cooked, or dried to add color, sweetness, and body to food.
The liquid pressed from carrots, used to add color, mild sweetness and natural vegetable flavor to foods and beverages.
The kernel of the fruit of the cashew tree, a tree nut. It is eaten as a snack or ground and used to add creaminess and nutty flavor.
Cauliflower is a vegetable made from the edible white flower head of the cauliflower plant. It is used as a food ingredient, either whole, puréed or dried into powder.
Cayenne pepper is a hot spice made by grinding the dried fruit of a red chili pepper. It is used to add heat and a reddish color to savory foods.
Celery is a crisp green vegetable from the stalks of a plant in the parsley family, and in food it adds a mild, fresh flavor and crunch.
Liquid pressed from celery stalks and leaves, used as a natural source of flavor and sometimes as a coloring or preservative ingredient in processed foods.
Dried and ground celery stalks and seeds, used as a natural source of flavor and as a curing agent that helps color and preserve meats.
Celery seed is the dried seed of the celery plant, ground or used whole to add a savory, slightly bitter flavor to seasonings.
A firm, aged cow's milk cheese with a sharp, tangy flavor, used in food for taste and texture.
Cheese is a solid food made by curdling milk, separating the curds from the whey, and aging or processing them. It adds flavor, texture and richness to foods.
Cherries are small stone fruits, used whole, chopped or as juice to add sweet-tart flavor and color.
The liquid pressed or extracted from cherries, used as a fruit-based flavoring and natural coloring in foods and drinks.
Chia seeds are small, oval seeds from the chia plant, a member of the mint family. In food they are used for their texture and their ability to absorb liquid and form a gel.
Chicken is the edible flesh of the domesticated bird, used as a meat ingredient that provides protein and savory flavor in food.
The lean muscle meat from the breast of a chicken, used as a protein ingredient in many prepared foods.
Chicken broth is a liquid made by simmering chicken meat, bones and sometimes vegetables in water, and it is used to add savory flavor to foods.
Fat rendered from the fatty tissue of chickens, used as a cooking and flavoring fat in foods such as baked goods and seasoning blends.
Chicken flavor is a flavoring made from chicken or chicken-derived compounds, used to give foods a chicken taste.
Meat from chickens, used as a protein and savory ingredient in the food it is added to.
Chickpeas are round, beige legume seeds that are cooked, roasted, or ground into flour. In packaged food they add texture, bulk and a mild, nutty flavor.
A pale, fine powder ground from dried chickpeas. It is used to thicken batters and doughs and to add protein and a mild nutty flavor to foods.
Chicory root fiber is a fiber extracted from the root of the chicory plant, consisting mainly of inulin. It is added to foods to increase fiber content and to provide bulk and mild sweetness.
Ground, roasted root of the chicory plant, often used as a coffee substitute or to add body and a roasted flavor.
The fruit of the chili pepper plant, used fresh, dried or ground. It is added to foods for heat and flavor.
Chipotle pepper is a smoked and dried ripe jalapeno pepper, ground or used whole, that adds smoky, moderately hot flavor to sauces, marinades, and seasonings.
Chives are the thin, hollow green leaves of a small onion-family plant, used to add a mild onion flavor and fresh green color to food.
A food made from roasted and ground cacao beans, combined with cocoa butter and often sugar. It provides a rich, sweet cocoa flavor.
Small pieces of chocolate made from cocoa solids, sugar, and fat, added to foods for flavor and texture.
Chocolate coating is a confectionery layer made from cocoa solids, sugar, and fats that is melted and applied over foods. It adds a sweet chocolate flavor and a crisp or glossy outer layer.
A form of vitamin D3, a fat-soluble vitamin added to foods to supply this nutrient.
A salt of the metal chromium combined with chloride, used as a source of the trace mineral chromium in food and supplement formulations.
A vinegar made by fermenting the sugars in crushed apples into alcohol and then into acetic acid. It is used for its sour, tangy flavor in dressings, sauces, and marinades.
The dried inner bark of tree species in the genus Cinnamomum, ground or rolled into sticks to add a sweet, warm spice flavor.
Cloves are the dried flower buds of an evergreen tree, used whole or ground as a spice for their warm, sharp aroma and flavor.
A layer of material applied over the outside of a food, such as sugar, batter or chocolate, to add flavor, texture or appearance.
A powder or paste made by roasting and grinding cacao beans after they have been fermented and dried, used to add chocolate flavor and color.
Cocoa butter is the natural fat extracted from cocoa beans during chocolate making. It gives chocolate its smooth melt and firm texture.
Chocolate liquor is a thick paste made by grinding roasted cacao beans, containing cocoa solids and cocoa butter, used as the base for chocolate and cocoa products.
A powder made from cacao beans after most of the cocoa butter is pressed out. It gives foods a deep chocolate flavor and brown color.
Dark cocoa powder made from cocoa beans treated with an alkali solution, which mellows its acidity and deepens its color.
Cocoa powder or cocoa solids that have been treated with an alkaline solution to reduce acidity and change color and flavor. It is used to make chocolate products darker and milder in taste.
Coconut is the fruit of the coconut palm, and in food it is used as the white flesh, milk, oil, or flakes to add sweet, nutty flavor and richness.
Thick, creamy liquid made by pressing the flesh of mature coconuts, used for richness and flavor in food.
Coconut milk is a liquid made by grating coconut meat and pressing it with water. It adds creamy texture and a coconut flavor to sauces, curries and desserts.
An oil pressed from the dried meat of coconuts, which is solid at room temperature and used for cooking, frying, and texture.
Coconut sugar is a sweetener made by evaporating the sap collected from coconut palm flower buds. It adds sweetness and a caramel-like flavor to foods.
Coconut water is the clear liquid found inside young green coconuts. It is used as a flavored base or mixer in beverages.
Coffee is the roasted and ground seed of the coffee plant, used to add its characteristic bitter, roasted flavor to foods and beverages.

A substance added to food to change or enhance its color, which may be derived from natural sources such as plants and minerals or made synthetically. It is used to make foods look more appealing or consistent.
Concentrated grape juice is grape juice with most of its water removed, leaving a thick, sweet liquid. It is used as a natural sweetener and for color in foods and drinks.
Concentrated lemon juice is lemon juice with most of its water removed, leaving a thick, tart liquid. It is used to add sourness and citrus flavor.
Pineapple juice concentrate is pineapple juice with most of its water removed, which makes it a thick syrup that adds sweetness and fruity flavor and is easier to store and ship.
Coriander is the dried seed of the cilantro plant, ground or whole. It is used as a spice to add a citrusy, warm flavor to foods.
Coriander leaves are the fresh green leaves of the coriander plant, also called cilantro, used as a herb to add a bright, citrusy flavor to food.
A cereal grain of the grass family, used whole, milled into flour or meal, or processed into starches and sweeteners.
Corn flour is a fine powder made by grinding dried corn kernels, used as a thickener and to provide structure in baked and processed foods.
Corn maltodextrin is a powdery starch derived from corn that is partly broken down by enzymes. It is used as a bulking agent, carrier and thickener in foods.
An oil extracted from the germ of corn kernels. It is used for frying, cooking and in processed foods as a fat.
A fine white powder extracted from corn kernels that is used to thicken sauces, bind ingredients and give foods a smooth texture.
Corn syrup is a sweet syrup made by breaking down cornstarch into glucose. It sweetens food and helps control texture and moisture.
The dried, concentrated solids of corn syrup, a sweetener made by breaking down corn starch into sugars, used in powdered and dry mixes.
Cornmeal is a coarsely ground powder made from dried corn kernels, used to add texture, body and a mild corn flavor to baked and fried foods.
Cottonseed is the seed of the cotton plant, and its oil is pressed from the seed and used as a cooking and processing oil in packaged foods.
Edible oil pressed from the seeds of the cotton plant, used for frying, baking and as an ingredient in processed foods.
A summer squash with thin green skin and pale flesh, used as a vegetable in cooked or processed foods for its mild flavor and texture.
Cranberries are small, tart red berries from a low-growing evergreen shrub, and in food they add a sour, fruity flavor and color.
Cream is the fatty layer of milk, rich in milk fat, that is used to add richness, smoothness and body to foods.
Cream cheese is a soft, mild white cheese made from cream or a mix of cream and milk, with a smooth, spreadable texture. It is used as a spread, filling, or ingredient in baked goods and sauces.
Crushed tomatoes are tomatoes that have been broken into small pieces with their juice, used as a base for sauces, soups and other dishes.
Crust is the baked outer layer of bread, pie, or pizza, made from a dough or pastry of flour, fat, and water. In packaged foods it refers to the shell or base of the product.
Cucumbers are the fruit of a vining plant eaten as a crisp vegetable, used fresh, pickled or as a flavoring in foods.
Pasteurized milk that has been inoculated with bacterial cultures and allowed to ferment, used as a base ingredient in products like cultured dairy foods, where it adds tang and a thicker texture.
The dried, ground seed of a plant in the parsley family with a warm, earthy flavor. It is used as a spice to season savory foods.
Cyanocobalamin is a synthetic form of vitamin B12, a water-soluble vitamin added to foods to supply this nutrient.
Alpha tocopherol acetate is the esterified form of vitamin E, a synthetic compound added to foods as a stable source of vitamin E and as an antioxidant that helps slow fat oxidation.
A type of chocolate made from cocoa solids, cocoa butter and sugar, with a higher proportion of cocoa than milk chocolate and little or no milk added. It has a rich, slightly bitter flavor.
Dates are the sweet, soft fruit of the date palm, dried or pressed into a paste. In food they add natural sweetness, moisture and a chewy texture.
Onion that has been cut and dried into small pieces or powder, used to add concentrated onion flavor to dry mixes and seasonings.
A simple sugar made from starch, most often corn, that is about as sweet as table sugar and adds sweetness and browning to foods.
Diced tomatoes in tomato juice are tomatoes cut into small cubes and packed in their own juice, used as an ingredient in sauces, soups and stews.
A condiment made from ground mustard seeds mixed with white wine or vinegar, often with salt and spices, giving it a sharp, tangy flavor used to season and flavor foods.
A feathery green herb with a fresh, slightly tangy flavor, using its leaves and seeds to season foods such as pickles, fish and sauces.
Distilled vinegar is a sour liquid made by fermenting ethanol into acetic acid, then distilling it to remove color and impurities. It is used to add tartness and act as a preservative in foods.
Synthetic form of vitamin E, added as an antioxidant to help keep fats and oils from going rancid.
Apple pieces with most of their water removed by drying, used as a chewy, sweet ingredient in snacks and cereals.
Dried garlic is the bulb of the garlic plant that has been dehydrated and ground, used as a seasoning to add garlic flavor to food.
A coarsely ground flour milled from durum wheat, a hard variety of wheat that gives pasta its firm texture and golden color.
Coarsely ground flour milled from hard durum wheat, commonly used to make pasta and couscous because it holds its shape when cooked.
Eggs are the whole eggs of hens, used to bind ingredients, add structure, enrich texture and contribute to leavening.
The clear, protein-rich part of eggs, used to add structure, foam, and binding to foods.
The yellow center portion of chicken eggs, used for its fat and protein to add richness, emulsify and bind ingredients.
A substance that helps oil and water mix together evenly and keeps a food's texture smooth and consistent. Common emulsifiers in food include lecithin, mono- and diglycerides, and polysorbates.

Proteins produced by living cells, often microbes, that act as catalysts to speed up specific chemical reactions in food. They are used to break down or build up components such as starches, proteins and fats during processing.
A form of vitamin D2 made by irradiating ergosterol, a compound found in yeast and fungi, and added to foods to boost their vitamin D content.
Evaporated cane juice is sugar cane juice that has been boiled down to dryness, leaving a granulated sugar that is sweetening and adds some natural flavor.
A cold-pressed oil obtained from olives by mechanical means alone, with no heat or chemical solvents, used as a fat for cooking and dressings and for flavor.
Fat is a general term for edible oils or animal fats used in food. It adds richness, texture and helps carry flavor and cooking heat.
Ferric orthophosphate is an iron compound made from iron and phosphate, added to fortify foods with iron and to act as a leavening agent.
Iron salt made by combining iron with sulfuric acid, used as a mineral fortificant to add iron to foods.
A soft, crumbly white cheese traditionally made from sheep's milk or a mix of sheep's and goat's milk, brined and used for its tangy flavor.

Filling is a prepared mixture of ingredients, such as fruit, cream, or starch-thickened blends, used to fill or stuff baked goods and snacks. It gives the product its inside layer of flavor and texture.
Water that has been passed through a filter to remove particles and impurities. It is used as a base for beverages, sauces and other foods.
A blend of natural or synthetic compounds that gives a food its distinctive taste or aroma, listed collectively without naming each component.
Flaxseed is the small, oil-rich seed of the flax plant, and it is added to foods for its nutty flavor, crunch and fiber.
A powder made by grinding dried grains, seeds or legumes, most often wheat. It is used as the main structural ingredient in breads, baked goods, pastas and many other foods.
Flour treatment agent is a substance added to flour to improve its baking performance, such as by whitening it or strengthening its dough.
Folic acid is a synthetic form of vitamin B9, a water-soluble vitamin added to foods to supply this nutrient.
Wheat flour that has had certain vitamins and minerals, such as iron and B vitamins, added back after milling. It serves as the main structural ingredient in baked goods and pasta.
The high-fat layer skimmed from cow's milk, with a fat content of about 36 percent, used to add richness and body to sauces, desserts and soups.
Fructose is a simple sugar found naturally in fruit and honey, and it is added to food as a sweetener.
Fruit is the edible, seed-bearing part of a plant, such as apples, berries or citrus, and it adds natural sweetness, flavor, moisture and color to food.
The liquid pressed or extracted from fruit, used as a natural sweetener and flavoring in foods and drinks.
A natural carbohydrate fiber extracted from the peels and pulp of fruit, most often apples or citrus. It is used to thicken and gel foods such as jams and jellies.
Garlic is a pungent bulb from the allium plant family, used fresh, dried or powdered. It adds savory flavor to food.
A dried, ground form of garlic bulbs that gives a concentrated garlic flavor without the moisture of fresh garlic. It is used as a seasoning in savory foods.
Garlic that has been crushed or blended into a smooth paste, used to add concentrated garlic flavor to sauces, marinades and seasoned foods.
The underground rhizome of a tropical plant, used fresh, dried or ground. It is added to foods for its pungent, spicy flavor.
Dried roots of the ginger plant ground into a fine powder, used as a spice to add warm, pungent flavor.
A simple sugar, also called dextrose, that is found naturally in fruits and plants and is often produced from corn starch. It is used to add sweetness, bulk, and browning to foods.
Glucose-fructose syrup is a sweetener made by breaking down corn or other starch into glucose and fructose, which is used to add sweetness and moisture to foods.
A thick, sweet liquid made by breaking down starch from corn, wheat, or other grains, used to add sweetness, body, and moisture to foods.
Graham flour is a whole-wheat flour made from the entire wheat kernel, coarsely ground, used in baked goods to give them a nutty flavor and coarse texture.
Grain vinegar is a sour liquid made by fermenting cereal grains such as corn or wheat into acetic acid, used to add tartness and preserve flavor.
Grapes are the fruit of the grapevine, used whole, as juice, or as a sweetening and flavoring ingredient in foods.
Green beans are the young, edible pods of the common bean plant, eaten whole as a vegetable. In packaged food they are used as a cooked or canned vegetable component.
The unripe fruit of the sweet pepper plant, with a crisp texture and a mildly bitter, vegetal flavor, used fresh or in cooked dishes and sauces.
Green chiles are unripe chili peppers, usually from the Capsicum genus, that are used to add mild to moderate heat and a fresh, vegetal flavor to foods.
Green peas are the mature seeds of the pea plant, harvested while green and often dried or frozen. They are used as a vegetable and add protein and texture to foods.
The unripe fruit of pepper plants, eaten as a vegetable and used fresh or cooked in many dishes.
Green tea is the dried, minimally processed leaves of the tea plant. It is used to add a mild, grassy flavor and characteristic color to foods and drinks.

Green tea extract is a concentrated preparation made from the leaves of the green tea plant, obtained by extracting them with water or solvent. It is used to add tea flavor and natural plant compounds to foods.
The insoluble, chewy base that forms the body of chewing gum, made from synthetic or natural polymers.
A type of hot chili pepper with a fruity flavor and strong heat, used to add spice and flavor to sauces and seasonings.
Ham is cured meat from the hind leg of a pig, salted or treated with curing agents and often smoked or cooked, used as a savory meat ingredient.
The edible nut of the hazel tree, with a round, smooth shell and a rich, buttery flavor. It is used whole, chopped, or ground in foods and is often paired with chocolate.
Leafy plant parts such as parsley, basil, oregano or thyme, used fresh or dried to add aromatic flavor and color to food.
A liquid sweetener made from corn starch that has been processed so that part of its glucose is converted to fructose, giving a sweet, stable syrup.
Oil pressed from sunflower seeds that has been bred to contain a high proportion of monounsaturated oleic acid. It is used for frying, baking and as a cooking oil.
Salt mined from ancient deposits in the Himalayan foothills, with trace minerals that give it a pinkish color.
Honey is a sweet syrup produced by bees from flower nectar, used to sweeten foods and add flavor and moisture.
A pungent root vegetable of the mustard family, ground or grated and used as a sharp, spicy seasoning.

Hydrogenated palm kernel oil is an oil pressed from the kernel of the oil palm fruit that has been treated with hydrogen to make it more solid at room temperature. In food it is used as a fat that gives structure and a firm texture.
A fat made from plant oils that have been treated with hydrogen so they stay solid at room temperature, used to add texture and extend shelf life.

Hydrolyzed corn protein is protein from corn that has been broken into smaller pieces, or peptides and amino acids, using water and enzymes or acids. In food it is used to add savory flavor and enhance taste.
A protein ingredient made by breaking soybean protein into smaller pieces with water and enzymes or acids, used to add savory flavor and texture to foods.
Finely ground powdered sugar, usually made from refined cane or beet sugar with a small amount of anti-caking starch, used to sweeten and thicken icings, frostings and dusting.
Inositol is a sugar-like compound that is a type of cyclic alcohol, found naturally in many plants and animal tissues. In food it is used as a sweetener, texturizer, or nutritional additive.
A soluble fiber naturally found in plants such as chicory root and agave. It is added to foods to add bulk, sweetness or a creamy texture.
A sweet syrup of glucose and fructose created by breaking down sucrose with an acid or enzyme. It keeps foods moist, resists crystallization, and adds sweetness.
A sweet liquid made by splitting sucrose into glucose and fructose, which keeps sugar from crystallizing and adds sweetness and moisture.
Iodized salt is table salt, sodium chloride, with a small amount of iodine added, used for seasoning and as a source of this mineral.
A mineral that is added to foods as a nutrient. In food it is typically used in forms such as ferrous fumarate or elemental iron powder to fortify cereals and other products.
A green chili pepper of medium heat, used whole, sliced, or diced to add spicy flavor to foods.
The liquid extracted by pressing or squeezing fruit or vegetables, used as a flavoring and sweetener in the product.
Kale is a leafy green vegetable from the cabbage family. In food it is used as a leafy vegetable ingredient, adding color and a slightly bitter flavor.
An enzyme produced by microorganisms that breaks down lactose, the sugar in milk, into simpler sugars in dairy products.
A mixture of lactic acid-producing bacteria added to foods such as yogurt, cheese and fermented products, where they convert sugars into lactic acid to develop tartness and aid texture.
A bacterium of the lactic acid bacteria group, cultured for use as a starter in fermented dairy and other foods, where it produces lactic acid and contributes to flavor and texture.
A bacterial strain used as a starter culture to ferment milk into yogurt, where it converts lactose into lactic acid and gives the product its tangy flavor and texture.
A type of lactic acid bacteria added to foods such as yogurt and cheese, where it produces acid and contributes to flavor and texture.
Lactose is a natural sugar found in milk, made of glucose and galactose, and it adds mild sweetness and helps browning in foods.
Lemon is the fruit of the lemon tree, used for its juice, zest or oil. It adds sour, bright citrus flavor to foods and drinks.
The liquid pressed from lemons, used for its sour, tart flavor. It is also used to adjust acidity and help preserve color in foods.
Lemon juice from concentrate is juice from lemons that has had most of its water removed and was later reconstituted with water, used to provide tart citrus flavor.
Lemon oil is the aromatic oil pressed from lemon peel, used to give foods and beverages a fresh lemon flavor and aroma.
Lemon peel is the thin outer skin of lemons, grated or dried, used to add bright citrus aroma and flavor.
A tall, fibrous tropical grass whose pale lower stalks are used as a fragrant herb, giving a bright, citrusy flavor to soups, curries and teas.
Lime is the small, green, acidic citrus fruit, used as juice or zest to add sour, bright flavor.
Juice pressed from limes, a citrus fruit, used to add tart citrus flavor and acidity to foods and drinks.
Lime juice concentrate is lime juice with most of its water removed, used to provide tart citrus flavor in beverages and other foods.
Liquid sugar is sugar, typically sucrose, dissolved in water to form a syrup. It is easy to blend into beverages and other foods and sweetens them.

Low-moisture part-skim mozzarella is a semi-soft cheese made from cow's milk with some of the milk fat removed and less water retained. It is used for melting and stretching in foods like pizza and snacks.
The edible seeds of a tree native to Australia, with a buttery, mildly sweet flavor, used whole or chopped in snacks, baked goods and confections.
Malt is barley grain that has been germinated and then dried, used to provide a sweet, toasty flavor and to supply enzymes and sugars for fermentation and baking.
Malt extract is a thick, sweet syrup made by soaking and drying sprouted barley and then concentrating the liquid, used to add flavor, color and sweetness to foods and baked goods.
A thick, sweet syrup made by soaking barley in water so it sprouts, then drying and concentrating the resulting liquid. It is used as a sweetener and flavoring in baked goods and cereals.
Barley grain that has been germinated and then dried and roasted, used to add a malty flavor and color to foods and drinks.

A white powder made by partially breaking down corn, rice, wheat or potato starch into short chains of sugar units. It is used to add bulk, body and a mild sweetness to foods without adding much flavor.
A white crystalline mineral salt of manganese and sulfuric acid, used as a nutritional supplement to add manganese to food.
A tropical stone fruit with sweet, juicy orange flesh, used in food as fresh fruit, puree, or dried pieces.
Mangoes that have been pureed into a smooth, thick pulp, used to add fruit flavor and sweetness to foods.
Maple sugar is a granulated sweetener made by evaporating the sap of maple trees until it crystallizes and is dried. It is used to add sweetness and a maple flavor.
A sweetener made by boiling down the sap of sugar maple trees until it thickens. It adds a distinctive sweet, woody flavor to foods.
Margarine is a spreadable fat made mainly from plant oils that are partly hardened, used in place of butter for spreading and baking.
A soft, spongy confection made by whipping sugar or corn syrup with gelatin or egg white and a gelling agent, used for its light texture and sweetness.
Mayonnaise is an emulsion of oil, egg yolk and an acid such as vinegar or lemon juice. It is used as a creamy spread or binder that adds richness and tang.
Microbial enzymes are proteins produced by bacteria, fungi or yeast that are used to speed up specific chemical reactions, such as helping milk curdle in cheesemaking.
Active cultures are live microorganisms, typically bacteria, added to foods such as yogurt to ferment them and develop flavor and texture.
Milk is the liquid produced by mammary glands, here from cows, containing water, fat, protein and sugar, used as a base for many foods.
Milk chocolate is a confection made from cocoa solids, sugar, milk solids and cocoa butter, and it gives foods a creamy, sweet chocolate flavor.
Milk powder is dairy milk that has been dried into a fine powder, used to add milk flavor, creaminess, and body to foods without liquid.
Milk protein concentrate is a dry powder made by removing most of the water and lactose from skim milk, leaving a higher proportion of milk proteins. It is used to add body and texture to foods.
A concentrated, dried form of the protein found in milk, produced by removing most fat, lactose and other components, used to add protein and structure.
The protein fraction obtained from milk, used to add protein, texture, and creaminess to foods. It is often dried into a powder for use in beverages, bars, and dairy-style products.
The fat portion separated from cow's milk, which is the component that gives butter and cream their richness. It is used to add flavor, richness, and a smooth texture to foods.
A group of small-seeded grains from grasses, cooked and eaten whole or ground into flour, and used in cereals and baked goods.
Mineral compounds, such as calcium, iron, or zinc salts, that are added to fortify foods with nutrients.
Mixed condiments is a blend of seasonings and flavorings, such as spices, herbs and sauces, combined to add flavor to a food product.

Corn starch that has been chemically or physically treated to change how it thickens, holds water or behaves under heat and acid. It is used to stabilize texture in sauces, dressings, soups and fillings.
Modified potato starch is starch extracted from potatoes and chemically or physically altered, used to thicken, stabilize texture or improve how foods hold together.

Starch from a plant source that has been chemically or physically modified to alter its thickening, stability or texture properties. It is used to thicken, stabilize and give body to foods such as sauces, soups and dairy products.

Modified tapioca starch is starch extracted from the cassava root and chemically or physically altered to change its properties. In food it acts as a thickener and stabilizer that helps texture hold up during processing.
Modified wheat starch is wheat starch that has been chemically or physically altered to change its thickening, texture or stability, used to thicken and bind foods.
A thick, dark syrup left over after sugar is extracted from sugarcane or sugar beets, used to add sweetness and a rich, slightly bitter flavor.
A natural sweetener made from the juice of the monk fruit, a small melon-like fruit, concentrated into an extract. It is used as a sugar substitute with almost no calories.
Monterey Jack cheese is a semi-hard, mild white cheese made from cow's milk. In food it adds creamy, mild flavor and melts smoothly.
A soft, mild, white cheese traditionally made from cow's or buffalo's milk. It melts and stretches when heated, which makes it common on pizza and in baked dishes.
Muesli is a breakfast mix of rolled oats, grains, nuts, and dried fruit, usually eaten with milk or yogurt. It provides texture, bulk, and a mix of flavors and crunch.
An edible fungus, cultivated or foraged, that is used as a vegetable in cooking. It adds earthy flavor and a soft, meaty texture to foods.
The seeds of mustard plants, ground and used as a spice, or a prepared condiment made from them, which adds sharp flavor.
Small seeds of the mustard plant, ground or whole, used as a spice and as the base for prepared mustard condiments.
A blend of flavoring compounds, some derived from natural sources such as plants or animals and some made synthetically, that are added to give a food its taste or smell.
Colorant derived from natural sources such as plants, fruits, vegetables or minerals, used to give food a color.
Natural flavor is a flavoring derived from a natural source such as plant, animal or microbial material. It adds taste or aroma to food.
Natural smoke flavor is a flavoring derived from wood smoke that has been captured and concentrated, used to give foods a smoky taste.
Natural vanilla flavor is a flavoring obtained from vanilla beans through extraction, usually with alcohol or water. It is added to foods to give a sweet, vanilla taste.
Oil pressed from canola seeds, a variety of rapeseed bred for low levels of certain compounds. It is used for cooking, frying, and as a base in dressings and baked goods.
Nutmeg is the dried, ground seed of the nutmeg tree, used as a warm, aromatic spice to flavor baked goods, sauces, and beverages.
Cereal grain from the oat plant, used whole, rolled, or milled into flour to provide texture, bulk, and a mild flavor.
Oat bran is the outer layer of the oat grain, separated from the rest of the kernel during milling. It is used as a source of fiber and to add a mild, nutty flavor and texture.
Insoluble fiber obtained from the outer hulls of oats, used to add bulk and texture to foods.
Oat flakes are oat grains that have been steamed and flattened into thin pieces, used as a cereal base and to add texture to baked goods.
Oat flour is a fine powder made by grinding whole oats or oat groats into a flour used to add bulk, texture, and mild flavor to baked goods and cereals.

Oil is a general term for a fat that is liquid at room temperature, typically extracted from plants or seeds and used for cooking and as a base in foods. The specific source is usually named on the label when it matters.
The fruit of the olive tree, pressed or cured for eating, and used whole or as an ingredient for its flavor and texture.
Olive oil is a fat pressed from the fruit of the olive tree, and in food it is used for cooking, dressings, and to carry flavor.
Onion is the bulb of a plant in the allium family, used fresh, dried or powdered. It adds savory flavor and aroma to food.
Onion powder is onions that have been dehydrated and ground into a powder, used to add savory onion flavor to seasonings and prepared foods.
Orange is a citrus fruit, and its juice or pulp is used to add sweet, tangy citrus flavor to foods and beverages.
Liquid pressed from oranges, a citrus fruit, used as a natural sweet and tangy juice ingredient in beverages and foods.
The outer colored layer of orange peel, grated or dried and used to add citrus aroma and flavor to foods.
Oregano is a dried herb from the mint family whose leaves are used to season foods with a warm, earthy, slightly bitter flavor.
Palm is oil obtained from the fruit of the oil palm tree, a semi-solid fat that is used to provide texture, stability and richness in foods.
A fat pressed from the kernel, or seed inside, of the oil palm fruit. It is solid at room temperature and is used to give baked goods and confectionery a firm texture and a long shelf life.
An edible fat pressed from the fruit of oil palm trees. It is used for its solid texture at room temperature and its stability in frying and baking.
A B-vitamin, also called vitamin B5, that is added to foods as a nutrient. It is typically a white powder or a pale yellow oil.
The sweet, orange-fleshed fruit of a tropical tree, eaten fresh or used in juices, purees and desserts, and sometimes processed into a tenderizing enzyme extract.
Paprika is a powder ground from dried fruit of the sweet pepper plant, used to add mild, sweet red color and flavor.
Parmesan is a hard, aged cheese made from cow's milk, and in food it contributes a sharp, savory, salty flavor.
Parsley is a green leafy herb from the parsley plant, used fresh or dried. It adds a mild, fresh flavor and green color to foods.

Partially hydrogenated soybean oil is soybean oil that has been treated with hydrogen so that some of its fats become more solid, which helps it keep texture and shape in foods like spreads and baked goods.
Pasta is a dried or fresh dough made from wheat flour or semolina mixed with water and shaped into forms such as noodles or shells. It is a staple starch ingredient used in many prepared dishes.
Pasteurized milk is cow's milk that has been heated to a set temperature for a short time to reduce microorganisms, and it is used as a liquid ingredient for dairy flavor and moisture.
A dairy ingredient combining milk and cream that has been heat-treated to kill microbes, used to add richness, moisture and a creamy texture to foods.
Milk that has been heat-treated to kill microorganisms and had some of its fat removed, leaving a lower-fat dairy product that still contains some milk fat.
Milk that has had most of its fat removed and has been heat-treated, used as a base ingredient that adds protein, lactose and milk solids.
Small, round green seeds of a climbing legume plant, eaten fresh, frozen, or dried and used whole or ground in many dishes and products.
Pea protein is a protein ingredient extracted from yellow field peas by separating the protein from the starch and fiber. It is used to add protein content and texture to foods.
Peaches are the soft, juicy fruit of a tree in the rose family, with a fuzzy skin and sweet flesh around a single large pit. They are eaten fresh or used in canned, dried, and baked products.
Legumes that grow underground in pods, used whole, roasted, or ground into butter and flour to add nutty flavor and texture.
Peanut flour is made by grinding roasted peanuts after most of their oil has been pressed out. It adds peanut flavor and a dry, powdery texture to baked goods and other foods.
A pale oil pressed from peanuts that is used for frying and cooking. It adds a neutral flavor and helps food brown and crisp.
A spread made by grinding roasted peanuts into a smooth or chunky paste, often with salt and sweeteners added. It gives a creamy texture and nutty flavor to foods.
Pears are the fruit of the pear tree, and in packaged foods they are used as a fruit ingredient to add sweetness, flavor and moisture.
A sweetener made by evaporating most of the water from pear juice, leaving a thick syrup that adds natural fruit sweetness to food.
Pecans are the edible nuts of the pecan tree, used in food for their rich, buttery flavor and crunchy texture.
The dried, ground berry of a climbing vine native to India, with a sharp, hot flavor. It is used as a spice to season foods.
An essential oil obtained by steam distilling the leaves and flowering tops of peppermint plants, used to add a strong mint flavor.
Pepperoni is a cured, seasoned sausage made from pork and beef, flavored with paprika and other spices. It is commonly sliced and used as a topping or snack.
Pineapple is the fruit of the pineapple plant, here used in its fruit form or juice to add sweet-tart flavor.
Pineapple juice is the liquid pressed from ripe pineapple fruit, used to add sweet, tropical fruit flavor and moisture.
The dried, mottled seeds of a bean plant, which are rehydrated and cooked, and are used as a source of starch, protein and fiber in food.
Pistachios are the edible seeds of the pistachio tree, used whole or chopped. They add crunch, color and a mild nutty flavor to foods.
Popcorn is a special type of corn whose kernels expand into fluffy pieces when heated. In food it is used as a whole-grain snack or as a base for snack products.
Tiny seeds from the opium poppy plant, used whole as a crunchy topping or ground into baked goods and fillings.
Meat from domestic pigs, used as a protein ingredient in foods such as sausages, cured meats and ready meals.
Potatoes are the starchy tubers of the potato plant, used whole or as flour, flakes, or starch. In packaged foods they add bulk, texture, and starch.
Dried, thin flakes made from cooked and mashed potatoes. They are used to thicken soups and make instant mashed potatoes.
Potato flour is a fine powder made by drying and grinding whole potatoes, used to add body, thickness and starch to baked goods and mixes.
A starch extracted from potatoes, used to thicken, bind, and give foods a smooth texture.
Substances added to food to slow spoilage, such as by inhibiting mold, bacteria, or oxidation, and extend shelf life.
A semi-hard Italian cheese made from cow's milk, with a mild, slightly smoky flavor, often used in sandwiches and melted dishes.
Pumpkin is a winter squash whose flesh is cooked and pureed for use in food. It adds color, body and a mild, sweet flavor to baked goods and other products.
Pumpkin seeds are the flat, green seeds found inside pumpkins and other squash, usually hulled and roasted. In food they add crunch and a mild, nutty flavor.
A form of vitamin B6 made as a salt, used as a fortificant to add vitamin B6 to food.
Quinoa is the seed of the Chenopodium quinoa plant, a grain-like crop from the Andes. It is used whole, as flour, or puffed, and adds a mild, nutty flavor and a starchy texture.
Raisins are dried grapes that are added to food for their sweet, chewy texture and natural fruit flavor.
A group of ingredients, typically sodium bicarbonate combined with acid salts, that release gas when heated or mixed. They make baked goods rise and become lighter.
Oil pressed from rapeseed, a plant in the mustard family. It is used for cooking, frying, and in salad dressings and baked goods.
Small, soft, red berries from a bramble shrub, used fresh, frozen, or as puree, juice, and flavoring in foods and drinks.
A smooth, thick liquid made by cooking and pureeing raspberries. It adds fruit flavor, color, and sweetness to sauces, fillings, and beverages.
Red and green bell peppers are sweet peppers of two ripeness stages, used as vegetables or dried and ground into seasoning to add flavor and color.
The mild, sweet fruit of a pepper plant, typically dried and ground or used as a vegetable. It adds red color and mild flavor to foods.
Red cabbage is the leaves of a purple-hued variety of cabbage, used whole or as an extract to add color and some flavor to foods.
Red chili pepper is the dried or ground fruit of the chili plant, used to add heat and color to seasonings and sauces.
Red onion is a variety of onion with purple-red skin and flesh, used as a vegetable to add mild, sharp onion flavor to foods.
Red wine vinegar is a sour liquid made by fermenting red wine into acetic acid, used to add tang and acidity to foods.
Iron powder produced by chemical reduction that is added to fortify foods with a mineral and to help color them.
Set of enzymes, traditionally taken from the stomach lining of young animals, used to curdle milk in cheese making.
Retinyl acetate is a form of vitamin A, produced synthetically, that is added to foods to increase their vitamin A content.
A form of vitamin A produced by chemically combining retinol with palmitic acid. It is added to foods as a source of vitamin A.
A cereal grain from the rice plant that is used whole, milled or puffed. In packaged foods it provides bulk, crunch and a mild flavor.
A fine powder made by grinding milled rice grains, used as a thickener, binder, or base in baked goods and other foods.
A fine white powder made from the carbohydrate starch extracted from rice grains. It is used as a thickener and to give foods a smooth, crisp texture.
Rice syrup is a sweetener made by breaking down the starch in cooked rice with enzymes into simple sugars. It adds sweetness and body to foods.
A mild vinegar made by fermenting rice or rice wine, used to add a gentle tang to dressings, sauces and pickled foods.
A soft, fresh Italian cheese made from whey, often with some milk or cream, with a mild, slightly sweet flavor and grainy, creamy texture.
Roasted almonds are almonds that have been heated until golden, used to add a toasty, nutty flavor and crunchy texture.
Roasted peanuts are peanuts that have been heated until golden and fragrant, used whole or chopped to add nutty flavor and crunch.
Romaine lettuce is a variety of leafy green with long, sturdy, crisp leaves, used as a fresh vegetable in salads and other dishes.
A hard, salty Italian cheese made from sheep's milk that is aged and grated. It adds a sharp, savory flavor to dishes.
A fragrant herb from the mint family, dried and ground for use as a seasoning that adds a piney, savory flavor to foods.
Rye flour is a powder milled from the grain of rye, a cereal related to wheat. It provides structure and flavor in baked goods and breads.
Safflower oil is a vegetable oil pressed from the seeds of the safflower plant. It is used as a cooking and salad oil and as a fat ingredient in processed foods.
Salt is a mineral compound, mainly sodium chloride, mined or evaporated from seawater. It is used to season food and to enhance and preserve flavor.
A liquid mixture of ingredients such as tomatoes, spices, oils and thickeners that is poured or spread over food. It adds flavor and moisture to dishes.
Sea salt is salt obtained by evaporating seawater, usually containing small amounts of trace minerals. It seasons food and adds flavor.
Edible marine algae harvested from the sea and dried or processed, used as a vegetable or to add a savory, umami flavor and to thicken or gel foods.
Partially skimmed milk is cow's milk from which some of the cream has been removed, leaving a lower fat content while keeping most of the milk's other components.

Semisweet chocolate is a chocolate made from cocoa solids, cocoa butter and sugar, with less sugar than sweet chocolate. In food it provides a rich cocoa flavor and is used in baking and confectionery.
Semolina is the coarse, purified middle of durum wheat, milled from the endosperm. It is used to make pasta and some breads and gives products a firm, golden texture.
Sesame is the small oil-rich seed of the sesame plant, used whole, ground, or pressed for oil to add flavor and crunch.
Sesame oil is a pale, nutty-flavored vegetable oil pressed from sesame seeds, used for cooking, frying, and seasoning dressings and sauces.
Sesame seeds are the small seeds of the sesame plant, used whole or ground to add a nutty flavor and crunchy texture to food.
A small member of the onion family with mild, sweet garlic-like flavor, used chopped or minced to season sauces, dressings and savory dishes.
A small crustacean with a translucent shell that turns pink when cooked. It is eaten as seafood and has a mild, sweet flavor.
Milk with most or all of its fat removed, used as a source of milk solids, protein and moisture in foods and beverages.
Milk with most of its fat removed, then dried into a powder that adds milk solids, flavor, and texture to foods.
Smoke flavor is a flavoring made by capturing the condensed compounds from burning wood, which gives foods a smoky taste without actual smoking.
A mineral element found in table salt and many processed foods. In food it is used to add a salty taste and to help preserve and flavor products.
A milk protein derived from casein that has been combined with sodium. It is used to help bind ingredients, improve texture and keep mixtures from separating.
Sodium chloride is the chemical name for common salt, mined or produced from seawater. It seasons food and also helps preserve it and control texture.
Sodium citrate is the sodium salt of citric acid, a white powder used as a buffer to control acidity and help ingredients blend smoothly.
Sodium selenite is a white inorganic salt containing sodium and selenium. In food it is added as a source of the mineral selenium for nutritional fortification.

Soluble corn fiber is a carbohydrate fiber derived from corn starch that is processed into a form that dissolves in water. It is added to food to increase fiber content and bulk without changing texture much.
Sour cream is a dairy product made by culturing cream with lactic acid bacteria, giving a thick texture and tangy flavor.
Cultured milk is milk that has been fermented with bacterial cultures, which thickens it and gives it a tangy flavor.
Soy protein is a protein isolated from soybeans, used to add structure, texture and protein content to foods.
Soy protein isolate is a powder made from defatted soybeans with most of the carbohydrates removed, and it is used to add protein and help bind or texture foods.
A dark liquid condiment made by fermenting soybeans, wheat, salt, and water over several months. It adds a salty, savory, umami flavor to foods.
Soy is a legume, the soybean, whose seeds are processed into products such as flour, oil, protein, and sauces. In food it provides protein, texture, emulsification, or flavor.
The seed of the soybean plant, a legume. In packaged foods it appears as whole beans or as derived ingredients such as oil and flour.
A powder made by grinding dehulled soybeans into flour. It is used to add protein, bind ingredients and add texture to foods.
Soy lecithin is a fatty substance extracted from soybeans, containing phospholipids. It acts as an emulsifier, helping oil and water mix smoothly.
An edible oil pressed from soybeans that is used for frying, baking and as a cooking fat in many packaged foods.
Spices are aromatic parts of plants such as seeds, bark, roots or fruits, dried and ground. They add flavor and aroma to food.
A concentrated flavoring made by extracting aromatic compounds from spices using a solvent, used to add spice flavor to foods.
Spinach is a leafy green vegetable whose leaves are eaten fresh or cooked, adding mild flavor, color and bulk to foods.
Leaves of the spinach plant that have been dried and milled into a fine green powder, used to add color and a mild vegetable flavor to foods.
Young onion harvested before the bulb forms, with long green leaves and a mild onion flavor, used fresh or cooked as a vegetable seasoning.
Water taken from an underground source that naturally flows to the surface, used as the base liquid in the product.
A substance such as a gum, starch or gelling agent that helps keep a food's texture, mixture or consistency uniform and stable.
Starch is a carbohydrate extracted from plants such as corn, potatoes or wheat. It is used to thicken, bind and give texture to foods.
The sweet red berry of a low-growing plant in the Fragaria genus. It is eaten fresh or used as fruit pieces, purée, or flavoring in foods such as jams, yogurts, and desserts.
Strawberry juice that has been concentrated by removing most of its water, used to add strawberry flavor and color.
Strawberry puree is strawberries that have been cooked or blended into a smooth pulp, used to add strawberry flavor, color and moisture to foods.
A type of lactic acid bacteria used to ferment milk, helping to produce yogurt and cheese and to give them their texture and tang.
Sucrose is the common table sugar extracted from sugar cane or sugar beets, used to add sweetness and bulk to foods.
Sugar is a sweet carbohydrate, usually extracted and refined from sugar cane or sugar beets. It sweetens food and adds bulk and browning in cooking.
Seeds from the sunflower plant, or oil pressed from them, used as a nutty-flavored ingredient or as a cooking and salad oil.
A natural emulsifier obtained from sunflower seeds, made of phospholipids. It helps oil and water mix evenly in foods such as baked goods and sauces.
Sunflower oil is a vegetable oil pressed from the seeds of the sunflower plant, used for frying, baking and as a cooking fat.
The edible seeds of the sunflower plant, eaten whole or ground, that add crunch, flavor, and fat to foods.
Sweet potato is a starchy tuberous root vegetable with orange or purple flesh. In food it is used as a vegetable, and its flesh can add sweetness and color to products.
Sweetened condensed milk is milk with most of its water removed and sugar added. It is thick and sweet and is used in desserts, candies and sauces.
Tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds. It adds a nutty flavor and creamy texture to sauces, dressings and spreads.
Tamari soy sauce is a dark, rich soy sauce brewed mainly from soybeans with little or no wheat, used to add salty, savory umami flavor to foods.
The pulp of the tamarind pod, a sour-sweet fruit, used to add tartness to sauces, candies and beverages.
A starch extracted from the root of the cassava plant, used to thicken, bind and give a chewy texture to foods.
A starch-derived ingredient made by heating tapioca starch with acid or heat to break it into smaller carbohydrate chains. It is used as a thickener, bulking agent, or texture modifier in foods.
Tapioca flour is a fine white starch extracted from the root of the cassava plant, used to thicken and add a chewy texture.
A sweetener made by converting the starch in tapioca root into a thick, sugary liquid. It adds sweetness and moisture to foods and is often used in place of corn syrup.
A sulfur-containing amino acid, originally isolated from ox bile, that is made synthetically and added to some foods and drinks, often in energy beverages.
Tea is the dried leaves of the Camellia sinensis plant, prepared by steeping in hot water. It is used as a source of flavor and aroma in beverages and other foods.
Textured vegetable protein is a protein ingredient made from soy or other plant sources that has been processed into a meat-like texture, used as a filler or meat substitute.
A water-soluble B vitamin, also called thiamine, that is involved in converting carbohydrates into energy. In food it is added to fortify cereals, breads and other grain products.
Thiamin hydrochloride is a salt form of vitamin B1, a manufactured compound added to foods to replace or fortify the thiamin they contain.
A form of vitamin B1 (thiamine) bonded with nitrate. It is added to foods as a source of thiamin.
Thyme is a fragrant herb from the mint family whose dried or fresh leaves are used to add an earthy, savory flavor to foods.
The fleshy red fruit of the tomato plant, used whole, chopped or as a purée. It adds sweetness, acidity and body to sauces and other dishes.
Tomato paste is tomatoes that have been cooked down and strained to a thick, concentrated puree. It is used to add tomato flavor, color, and body to sauces and soups.
The liquid obtained by crushing and straining ripe tomatoes. It is used as a base for sauces, soups and beverages, adding color and a tomato flavor.
A thick, smooth liquid made by cooking and straining tomatoes, used as a base for sauces, soups and other dishes.
A smooth sauce made from cooked and strained tomatoes, often seasoned with herbs and salt, used as a base for cooking and flavor.
Torula yeast is a single-celled fungus grown on sugar or molasses and then dried into a powder. It is used as a savory flavoring ingredient with a meaty or cheesy taste.
A group of edible seeds from trees such as almonds, walnuts, cashews and pecans, used whole, chopped or ground in food.
Turkey is a bird whose meat is used as a main ingredient in food, providing protein, texture and flavor in products like sausages and deli meats.
The breast cut of the turkey bird, used as a lean meat ingredient that supplies protein and a mild poultry flavor in processed foods.
Turmeric is a yellow spice made by drying and grinding the root of the turmeric plant. It is used to add a warm, earthy flavor and a bright yellow color to foods.
Butter made from churned cream with no salt added, used as a fat that contributes richness, flavor and a creamy texture to baked goods and sauces.
Vanilla is a flavoring extracted from cured seed pods of orchids in the vanilla genus, and it gives foods a sweet, floral aroma and taste.
An extract made by soaking cured vanilla pods in alcohol and water, which draws out the flavor compounds that give vanilla its taste and aroma.
A flavoring made by extracting flavor compounds from vanilla beans or producing them through processing, used to give foods a sweet, vanilla taste and aroma.
Vanilla bean is the dried, cured pod of the vanilla orchid, scraped or ground to add its sweet, aromatic vanilla flavor.
A compound that gives vanilla its characteristic aroma, made synthetically or extracted from vanilla beans, and used to flavor baked goods, dairy, and confections.

Vegetables is a general term for edible plant parts such as roots, stems, leaves, and fruits eaten as savory food. In packaged products it refers to a mix of vegetable ingredients, adding flavor, color and nutrients.
A mixture of several vegetables, such as carrots, peas, and onions, combined into one ingredient. It adds flavor, color, and texture to soups, sauces, and prepared meals.
Vegetable broth is a savory liquid made by simmering vegetables in water, used to add a mild, rounded flavor to soups, sauces, and other dishes.

A solid fat made from refined vegetable oils, such as soybean or palm oil, that has been hydrogenated or processed to stay solid at room temperature. It gives baked goods and frostings a firm, smooth texture.
Liquid pressed from vegetables such as tomatoes, carrots, or beets, used for color, flavor, and as a component in beverages and sauces.
An edible oil obtained from one or a mix of plant sources, such as soybean, palm or sunflower, used as a cooking and baking fat.
Vegetable for color is a pigment obtained from vegetable sources, such as fruit or vegetable juices, used to give a food a desired color.
A sour liquid made by fermenting alcohol or other sugar-containing liquids with acetic acid bacteria. It is used to add tartness, preserve foods and balance flavor.
Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin, a group of compounds including retinol and carotenoids. It is added to foods as a nutrient fortificant and often appears as a palmitate or acetate ester.
Vitamin B12 is a water-soluble vitamin, also called cobalamin, that is added to foods as a nutrient supplement.
A water-soluble B vitamin, also called pyridoxine, that the body needs for protein metabolism. In food it is added to raise the vitamin B6 content of cereals, bars and other products.
Ascorbic acid, a form of vitamin C that is often produced synthetically, and is used as an antioxidant to slow browning and spoilage in foods.
A fat-soluble vitamin, also known as calciferol, that is added to foods to supply a nutrient the body makes when skin is exposed to sunlight.
Vitamin E is a group of fat-soluble compounds that are added to food as an additive, often to help protect fats and oils from spoiling.
A group of organic compounds that the body needs in small amounts, added to food to boost its nutrient content.
Walnuts are the edible seeds of the walnut tree, used whole or chopped to add crunch and a mild, rich flavor.
Water is the liquid used as a base or solvent in food. It dissolves and carries other ingredients and helps set the texture of a product.
A cereal grain from the wheat plant that is ground into flour. In a product it supplies starch, protein and structure for baked goods, pasta and other foods.
The outer layer of wheat kernels, separated from the flour during milling, that is rich in fiber and often added back to baked goods and cereals.
A powder milled from the grains of wheat that provides structure and bulk in baked goods, pastas and many other foods.
Wheat gluten is the protein fraction isolated from wheat flour, which forms an elastic network when moistened. It is used to give foods chewiness, structure, and binding.
Wheat starch is the starch component separated from wheat flour, a fine white powder that is used to thicken, bind, and add texture to foods.
The liquid left over after milk is curdled and strained during cheese making, and it is dried into a powder. It is used to add milky flavor, protein and body to foods.
Whey powder is dried whey, the liquid left over after milk is curdled during cheese making, used to add milk solids, protein and flavor.
Whey protein is a protein isolated from whey, the liquid left after milk is curdled during cheese making, and it adds body and structure to foods.
A protein concentrate made by filtering the liquid left over from cheese making, leaving a highly purified protein powder that adds protein and body to foods.
White beans are the dried seeds of a bean plant with a mild, creamy flavor, used whole or ground to add body and texture to foods.
A confection made from cocoa butter, sugar, milk solids and vanilla, containing no cocoa solids, which gives it a pale color and creamy flavor.
A clear, sour liquid made by fermenting and then distilling ethanol, producing a neutral acetic acid solution. It is used to add tartness and to help preserve foods.
White pepper is the seed of the pepper plant with its outer skin removed before drying and grinding, used as a mildly pungent spice in light-colored dishes.
A clear, sour liquid made by fermenting diluted ethanol with acetic acid bacteria, used to add tartness and as a preservative.
Wine made from white grapes that are fermented without their skins, giving it a pale color, and used to add acidity and flavor.
Whole eggs are the complete contents of eggs, including both the white and yolk, and they are used to add structure, moisture, richness and leavening to foods.
Oat groats that have been steamed and flattened into flakes, with the bran, germ, and endosperm all retained. They are used in cereals, baked goods, and granola.
The liquid produced by cows, with its fat content left intact, typically around 3.25 percent. It is used as a beverage and as an ingredient in dairy and baked products.
Milk that has had its water removed by drying into a powder, keeping its fat and milk solids. It is used to add milk flavor, richness and body to foods.

Whole grain wheat is wheat kernels with all three parts, the bran, germ and endosperm, left intact. In food it provides the base grain for flour and cereal products, adding texture and a nutty flavor.
Flour milled from the entire wheat kernel, including the bran, germ and endosperm. It adds structure and body to baked goods and other foods.
Whole grain oats are oat kernels milled with the bran, germ and endosperm all kept, so the full grain is included in the flour or flakes made from them.
Whole grain oat flour is flour made by grinding whole oat grains, including the bran and germ, and it adds body, texture and a mild nutty flavor to baked products.
An alcoholic beverage made by fermenting grape juice, used in cooking and in some foods to add acidity, aroma and depth of flavor.
A fermented, savory liquid condiment made from vinegar, molasses, anchovies, tamarind, spices and other flavorings, used to add tangy, umami flavor.
A single-celled fungus grown on sugars and then dried or deactivated. It is used to leaven bread and other baked goods and to add savory, rich flavor.
A concentrate made from yeast cells whose contents have been broken down and extracted. It is used to add savory, meaty flavor to foods.
A fine powder milled from dried yellow corn kernels. It is used as a thickener and to give baked and processed foods structure.
A cultured dairy food made by fermenting milk with bacterial cultures, giving it a thick texture and tangy flavor.
Zinc is a metallic mineral element that is added to foods as a compound. It is used as a nutrient ingredient in food formulations.
Zinc oxide is a white mineral compound made from zinc, added to food in small amounts as a source of zinc and as a nutrient supplement.
A white crystalline mineral salt of zinc and sulfuric acid, used as a nutritional supplement to add zinc to food.
